Industrial Processes Powered by Gravitational Energy Systems

This section presents the industrial applications that can be potentially supplied by a continuous electrical power source generated by the gravitational energy system.


  • Containerized Green Electricity Generation
    • Continuous off-grid electrical power production.
    • Replacement of diesel generators for remote installations.
    • Power supply for industrial equipment and critical infrastructure.
    • Baseload electricity for manufacturing facilities and microgrids.

  • Atmospheric Water Generation (AWG)
    • Electrical power for atmospheric water generators.
    • Production of potable water from ambient humidity.
    • Water supply for remote communities, agriculture and industrial processes.
    • Fully autonomous containerized water production.

  • Green Hydrogen Production
    • Electrolysis powered by continuous electrical energy.
    • Hydrogen production using purified water.
    • Oxygen recovery as an industrial by-product.
    • Hydrogen supply for mobility, chemical industries and energy storage.

  • Direct Air Carbon Capture (DAC)
    • Continuous electrical supply for CO₂ capture systems.
    • Atmospheric carbon dioxide concentration.
    • Carbon feedstock for synthetic fuel production.
    • Support for carbon management strategies.

  • Synthetic Fuel Production
    • Sabatier reactors producing renewable methane (e-methane).
    • Fischer–Tropsch synthesis producing e-crude, e-diesel and e-methanol.
    • Integration of green hydrogen and captured CO₂.
    • Production of renewable fuels for maritime, aviation and heavy industry.

  • Industrial Heat & Process Energy
    • Electrical heating systems.
    • Steam generation through electric boilers.
    • Heat pumps for industrial thermal processes.
    • Support for food processing and chemical manufacturing.

  • Water Treatment & Desalination
    • Reverse osmosis desalination plants.
    • Industrial wastewater treatment.
    • Ultrafiltration and purification systems.
    • Municipal drinking water production.

  • Data Centers & Digital Infrastructure
    • Continuous power supply for servers.
    • Edge computing facilities.
    • Telecommunication infrastructure.
    • AI computing clusters and cloud platforms.

  • Manufacturing & Industrial Automation
    • CNC machining centers.
    • Robotic production lines.
    • Industrial automation equipment.
    • Packaging and logistics systems.

  • Mining & Remote Industrial Sites
    • Autonomous electrical supply for mining operations.
    • Power for drilling, crushing and material handling.
    • Energy independence in isolated locations.
    • Reduction of diesel fuel logistics.

  • Agriculture & Food Production
    • Irrigation pumping systems.
    • Controlled-environment agriculture.
    • Cold storage and refrigeration.
    • Livestock and aquaculture facilities.

  • Smart Grid & Microgrid Integration
    • Containerized autonomous microgrids.
    • Industrial energy hubs.
    • Backup and resilient electrical infrastructure.
    • Hybrid integration with solar, wind and battery systems.

Industrial Perspective:
A continuous electrical power source can support a wide range of industrial processes, including electricity generation, water production, hydrogen production, carbon capture, synthetic fuel synthesis, manufacturing, digital infrastructure and autonomous microgrids.
The suitability of any specific application depends on the demonstrated performance, reliability, safety and regulatory compliance of the underlying power generation technology.

International electricity generation without license

Electricity generation regulations

Overview

We are considering a gravity-powered low-carbon electricity generation facility located in Albania and operated exclusively for internal self-consumption.

The intended installation is designed to operate completely independently from the Albanian public electricity grid and is not intended to import electricity from or export electricity to the public electricity network.

Electricity would be used exclusively to satisfy internal household, industrial or corporate electricity requirements within the installation or under the producer's control.

The Albanian electricity-sector framework regulates electricity generation, transmission, distribution, supply and participation in the electricity market. The Energy Regulator Authority (ERE) is responsible for the regulation and licensing of activities within the electricity sector.

Albania's current primary electricity-sector legislation includes Law No. 59/2026 on the Electricity Sector . ERE's current legislation page also identifies Law No. 24/2023 on the promotion of the use of energy from renewable sources.

For a completely isolated installation used only for internal self-consumption, We should distinguish electricity-market licensing requirements from construction, environmental, land-use, electrical safety, water-use and other authorisations that may apply to the physical installation.

Technical Information
Country Albania 🇦🇱
Technology Gravity-powered low-carbon electricity generation system
Operating Mode Completely off-grid / island operation
Public Grid Connection None intended
Electricity Import No
Electricity Export No
Electricity Sale No
Electricity Purchase No
Purpose Internal household, industrial and corporate self-consumption only
Electricity Market Participation No
Electricity Distribution to Third Parties No
Electricity Supply to Third Parties No

Grid Balancing Not applicable to a genuinely isolated installation that does not participate in the electricity market
Grid Connection Code Not applicable to a facility that has no physical connection to the public grid; electrical safety requirements may still apply
Administrative Requirements

We should not interpret the absence of a public-grid connection as an exemption from all Albanian administrative requirements.

The current Albanian electricity framework provides for electricity-generation licensing and other regulated electricity-sector activities. Whether a particular completely isolated self-consumption installation falls within a licensing requirement must be determined from the applicable provisions and the actual characteristics of the project.

Electricity-Sector Assessment
  • Electricity generation for the electricity market is subject to the Albanian electricity regulatory framework.
  • Electricity transmission and distribution are regulated activities.
  • Electricity supply and electricity trading are regulated activities.
  • Participation in the electricity market creates additional regulatory obligations.
  • A completely isolated self-consumption installation must be assessed separately from a grid-connected electricity generation facility.
  • We should obtain confirmation from the competent Albanian authority before treating a large installation as exempt from electricity-generation licensing.
Other Potential Administrative Requirements
  • Construction and building authorisations, where applicable.
  • Land-use and planning requirements.
  • Structural engineering requirements.
  • Electrical installation and safety requirements.
  • Fire-safety requirements.
  • Occupational health and safety requirements.
  • Environmental authorisations or environmental assessment, where applicable.
  • Water-use authorisations if the technology uses water resources.
  • Other permits or approvals depending on the location, technology and physical characteristics of the installation.
Measures to Reduce Licensing Risk

To maintain the project as a genuine private off-grid self-consumption installation, We recommend that the project be designed and operated so that:

  • The installation remains physically isolated from the Albanian public electricity network.
  • No electrical connection is established with the public transmission or distribution network.
  • No electricity is imported from the public grid.
  • No electricity is exported to the public grid.
  • No electricity is sold to third parties.
  • No electricity is purchased from the public grid.
  • No electricity-market participation is undertaken.
  • No electricity trading activity is undertaken.
  • No electricity supply activity is undertaken for third parties.
  • No electricity distribution network is operated for unrelated third parties.
  • Electricity is used exclusively for internal household, industrial or corporate requirements.
  • The installation operates permanently in island mode.
  • The electrical design prevents unintended energisation or export towards the public grid.
  • Technical documentation demonstrates the independent and isolated nature of the facility.
  • We maintain documentation showing that the facility does not participate in the Albanian electricity market.
Maximum Electrical Power
Identified regulatory capacity: 5 MW

We have identified an Albanian ERE generation-licence category covering electricity generation facilities with a general installed capacity under 5 MW.

ERE's published generation-licence documentation expressly describes a licence for electricity generation from power plants with a general capacity under 5 MW.

This 5 MW threshold should, however, be understood as a regulatory licensing category and not automatically as a general maximum electrical capacity applicable to every completely isolated self-consumption facility.

The fact that the proposed facility uses a gravity-powered low-carbon technology does not by itself establish a separate Albanian statutory capacity limit specifically applicable to this technology.

For a completely off-grid installation, We should therefore determine the applicable licensing treatment according to the actual operating configuration, including:

  • whether the installation is physically connected to the public electricity network;
  • whether electricity is exported to the public network;
  • whether electricity is supplied or sold to third parties;
  • whether the installation participates in the electricity market;
  • the installed electrical generation capacity;
  • the technology and characteristics of the generating equipment; and
  • the applicable construction, environmental, land-use, water and safety requirements.
Important: The identified 5 MW figure is the capacity associated with the published ERE generation-licence category under 5 MW. It should not be represented as a universal statutory maximum for every off-grid self-consumption installation without confirmation under the current Law No. 59/2026 and its implementing regulations.
References
  1. Law No. 59/2026 on the Electricity Sector — current Albanian primary legislation for the electricity sector.
  2. Energy Regulator Authority (ERE) — Albanian electricity-sector regulatory authority and licensing framework.
  3. Law No. 24/2023 — Promotion of the Use of Energy from Renewable Sources.
  4. ERE legislation concerning electricity-generation licensing and other electricity-sector licences.
  5. ERE secondary legislation concerning electricity licensing procedures and conditions.
  6. ERE electricity network codes and technical requirements applicable where a facility is connected to the public network.
  7. Applicable Albanian construction, planning, environmental, water-resource, electrical-safety and occupational-safety legislation.

Primary regulatory source: Energy Regulator Authority of Albania (ERE).

The applicable legal requirements may depend on the technology, installed electrical capacity, location, land status, environmental characteristics, water use, ownership structure and actual operating configuration of the installation.

Overview

We are considering a gravity-powered low-carbon electricity generation facility located in Andorra and operated exclusively for internal self-consumption.

The intended installation is designed to operate independently from the public electricity network, without importing electricity from or exporting electricity to the public electricity grid.

Electricity would be used exclusively for internal household, industrial or corporate electricity requirements under the control of the producer.

Andorran legislation expressly recognizes isolated electricity-generation installations. The Regulation governing electricity generation defines an "isolated installation" as a generation installation operating autonomously without a physical connection to the electricity distribution or transmission network and supplying one or more uses or activities.

The Andorran electricity-generation framework applies to electricity-generation installations using renewable energy sources, including installations operating autonomously, with a reference regulatory capacity of up to 2,000 kW.

We should nevertheless distinguish the electricity regulatory framework from construction, environmental, planning, electrical-safety and other administrative requirements that may apply to the physical installation.

Administrative Requirements

Andorra has a specific administrative framework for electricity-generation installations.

The Government provides an official procedure for the registration of new electricity-generation installations and for modifications or cancellation of existing installations.

Registration of the Generation Installation

The official Andorran procedure permits the formal registration of new electricity production installations.

The procedure is available to both natural persons and legal persons.

The Andorran Government maintains a national energy register for electricity-generation installations.

We should therefore not describe a qualifying electricity-generation installation as completely free from administrative registration merely because it is off-grid.

Capacity-Based Requirements

For installations with a power greater than 500 kW and less than or equal to 2,000 kW, the Andorran Government requires an administrative authorization.

The promoter must submit a report describing the electricity production, production profiles and environmental impact.

The Government's official procedure also identifies technical and environmental documentation requirements for installations above 20 kW.

These requirements are separate from the question of whether electricity is sold or injected into the public electricity network.

Other Potential Requirements
  • Construction and planning requirements.
  • Land-use requirements.
  • Electrical installation and safety requirements.
  • Environmental assessment requirements, where applicable.
  • Structural engineering requirements.
  • Fire-safety requirements.
  • Occupational health and safety requirements.
  • Water-related authorisations where the project uses water resources.
  • Other authorisations depending on the location and characteristics of the installation.
Measures to Reduce Licensing Risk

For a project intended to remain a genuinely isolated self-consumption installation, We recommend that the installation be designed and operated so that:

  • The installation has no physical connection to the public electricity distribution or transmission network.
  • Electricity is generated exclusively for internal consumption.
  • No electricity is exported to the public grid.
  • No electricity is imported from the public grid.
  • No electricity is sold to third parties.
  • No electricity is purchased from the public electricity network.
  • The installation does not participate in the electricity market.
  • The installation is operated as an isolated electricity system.
  • Electrical protection prevents accidental connection or energisation of the public network.
  • Technical documentation demonstrates the autonomous operating configuration.
  • The actual electricity-generation technology is correctly classified under the applicable Andorran energy legislation.
  • Where the system is intended to qualify as renewable generation, We verify that its primary energy source falls within the applicable definition of renewable energy.
Maximum Electrical Power
Applicable capacity threshold: 2,000 kW (2 MW)

Andorran Law 21/2018 on the promotion of the energy transition and climate change expressly permits the production of electricity from renewable energy sources for installations with a power of less than or equal to 2,000 kW .

The Regulation governing electricity generation applies to renewable electricity-generation installations that are connected to the electricity network or operate autonomously with a power of less than or equal to 2,000 kW.

The Andorran Government's official guidance also expressly states that renewable electricity-generation installations, whether connected to or isolated from the electricity network, may be developed up to 2,000 kW.

Installations with a power greater than 500 kW and less than or equal to 2,000 kW require administrative authorization and additional documentation.

Isolated generation installations with a power of 5 kW or less are expressly exempted from the application of the 2020 electricity-generation regulation.

Technology qualification: The 2,000 kW threshold is established for the Andorran regulatory framework applicable to electricity generation from renewable energy sources. We should therefore verify that the actual primary energy source of a proposed gravity-powered system qualifies as a renewable energy source under Andorran law before applying this renewable-generation threshold to the project.

Website classification:
2,000 kW (2 MW) for an electricity-generation installation falling within the Andorran renewable-generation framework.

Overview

We are considering a gravity-powered low-carbon electricity generation facility located in Austria and operated exclusively for internal self-consumption.

The intended installation is designed to operate independently from the public electricity network, without importing electricity from or exporting electricity to the public electricity grid.

Electricity would be used exclusively for internal household, industrial or corporate electricity requirements under the control of the producer.

Austrian electricity legislation regulates the generation, transmission, distribution, storage, aggregation and supply of electricity.

Since electricity-law implementation is divided between federal and provincial legislation, the administrative requirements for a generation installation depend in particular on the Austrian Bundesland in which the facility is located.

The federal Elektrizitätswirtschaftsgesetz (ElWG) provides the national framework for the electricity sector. Provincial electricity laws establish important requirements concerning the construction and operation of electricity-generation installations.

A completely isolated self-consumption installation must therefore be assessed separately from a grid-connected generation facility, while remaining subject to applicable construction, safety, environmental, planning and provincial electricity requirements.

Administrative Requirements

We should not treat an off-grid installation as automatically exempt from Austrian administrative requirements.

The Austrian electricity framework is divided between federal legislation and the electricity laws of the individual Bundesländer.

Federal Electricity Framework

The current federal Elektrizitätswirtschaftsgesetz (ElWG) regulates electricity generation, transmission, distribution, storage, aggregation and supply.

The federal legislation also establishes obligations concerning electricity-generation installations and their interaction with electricity networks.

For example, the current federal framework contains provisions concerning new electricity generation installations and technical controllability requirements for certain installations.

These federal provisions do not create a single nationwide exemption threshold for every isolated self-consumption facility.

Provincial Electricity Law

The applicable Austrian Bundesland must be identified before determining the precise electricity-law approval requirement.

Provincial electricity legislation can establish specific capacity thresholds for electricity-generation installations.

As an example, the current Upper Austrian electricity law exempts certain electricity-generation installations from electricity-law approval up to specified capacity thresholds.

In Upper Austria, "other electricity-generation installations" with an installed bottleneck capacity of up to 5 kW are listed among installations not requiring the electricity-law approval referred to in § 6(1).

This 5 kW threshold is a Upper Austrian provincial threshold and must not be presented as a nationwide Austrian limit.

Other Potential Administrative Requirements
  • Provincial electricity-law authorization or notification, where applicable.
  • Construction and building-law requirements.
  • Land-use and spatial-planning requirements.
  • Electrical safety requirements.
  • Fire-safety requirements.
  • Occupational health and safety requirements.
  • Environmental requirements.
  • Water-law authorization where the installation uses water resources.
  • Structural engineering requirements.
  • Additional requirements arising from the particular technology and site.
Measures to Reduce Licensing Risk

For a project intended to remain a genuinely isolated self-consumption installation, We recommend that:

  • The electricity-generation installation has no physical connection to the Austrian public electricity network.
  • No electricity is imported from the public grid.
  • No electricity is exported to the public grid.
  • No electricity is sold to third parties.
  • No electricity is purchased from the public grid.
  • No participation in electricity trading is undertaken.
  • No participation in electricity balancing or aggregation markets is undertaken.
  • Electricity is used exclusively for internal household, industrial or corporate self-consumption.
  • The installation operates independently in island mode.
  • Electrical protection prevents accidental connection to or energisation of the public grid.
  • The installation is documented as a private self-consumption facility.
  • The applicable electricity law of the specific Bundesland is verified before construction.
  • The project's construction, environmental, planning, water and safety requirements are independently verified.
Maximum Electrical Power
Austria-wide maximum: No single nationwide kW/MW threshold has been identified for a purely off-grid, self-consumption-only electricity-generation installation without the applicable electricity-law authorization.

Austrian electricity-law regulation is divided between federal legislation and the legislation of the nine Bundesländer.

Consequently, the exact capacity that can be operated without an electricity-law approval cannot be stated as one figure for the whole of Austria.

The applicable capacity threshold must be determined from the electricity law of the Bundesland in which the facility will be constructed.

Example: Upper Austria

Under the current Upper Austrian electricity law, certain electricity-generation installations are exempt from the electricity-law approval requirement.

For "other electricity-generation installations", the exemption identified in § 6(2) covers installations with an installed bottleneck capacity of up to 5 kW .

This figure applies to the specific Upper Austrian regulatory category and is not an Austria-wide maximum.

Website classification for Austria:

The maximum capacity for a gravity-powered electricity-generation facility without the applicable electricity-law authorization must be determined at Bundesland level.

Example identified: Upper Austria — 5 kW for the specified category of "other electricity-generation installations" exempt from the electricity-law approval requirement.

We should therefore not enter "5 kW" as the Austrian national figure in the comparative table. We should instead identify the relevant Bundesland and apply that Bundesland's current electricity-law threshold.

References
  1. Elektrizitätswirtschaftsgesetz (ElWG), BGBl. I Nr. 91/2025 — current federal Austrian electricity-sector framework.
  2. ElWG § 2 — scope covering electricity generation, transmission, distribution, storage, aggregation and supply.
  3. ElWG § 74 — obligations applicable to electricity generators.
  4. ElWG § 76 — technical controllability requirements for certain new or substantially modified electricity-generation installations.
  5. Erneuerbaren-Ausbau-Gesetz (EAG) § 82 — self-consumption and generation outside the public electricity network.
  6. Elektrizitätsabgabegesetz — treatment of electricity generated and consumed by electricity producers themselves, including renewable self-consumption.
  7. Oö. Elektrizitätswirtschafts- und -organisationsgesetz 2006 § 6 — Upper Austrian electricity-generation approval requirements and exemptions, including the 5 kW threshold for certain "other electricity-generation installations".
  8. Applicable electricity legislation of the Bundesland in which the proposed installation will be constructed.

Overview

We are considering a gravity-powered low-carbon electricity generation facility located in Belarus and operated exclusively for internal self-consumption.

The intended installation is designed to operate independently from the public electricity network, without importing electricity from or exporting electricity to the public electricity grid.

Electricity would be used exclusively for internal household, industrial or corporate electricity requirements under the control of the producer.

Belarus maintains a regulated electricity sector in which electricity generation, energy supply and electricity-network activities are subject to specific statutory and regulatory requirements.

The current Belarusian Law on Licensing establishes the types of activity subject to licensing and provides an exhaustive framework for determining which activities require a licence.

For the specific configuration considered here, namely a physically isolated generation facility producing electricity exclusively for its own internal consumption, We have not identified a Belarusian statutory provision establishing a specific kW or MW threshold applicable solely to this configuration.

The absence of an identified numerical threshold should not be interpreted as an automatic exemption from all Belarusian administrative requirements. Construction, electrical safety, environmental, industrial-safety, land-use and other requirements may apply according to the characteristics of the installation.

Administrative Requirements

We should distinguish the electricity-market licensing framework from the other administrative requirements applicable to the physical installation.

Electricity Licensing

The Belarusian Law of 14 October 2022 No. 213-Z "On Licensing", as amended, establishes the legal framework governing licensing and determines the list of licensed types of activity.

The law states that only activities included in its prescribed list of licensed activities are subject to licensing.

We have not identified, in the sources reviewed, a provision establishing a specific electricity-generation licence requirement based solely on the existence of a physically isolated generator producing electricity exclusively for its own internal consumption.

The exact legal classification should nevertheless be confirmed for the particular installation before construction or operation.

Self-Consumption Configuration

The proposed configuration should remain strictly limited to internal consumption.

  • Electricity is consumed by the producer.
  • Electricity is not sold to third parties.
  • Electricity is not supplied through the public electricity network.
  • Electricity is not exported to the public electricity network.
  • Electricity is not purchased from the public electricity network.
  • The generating installation remains physically isolated from the public electricity network.
Other Potential Administrative Requirements
  • Construction and building requirements.
  • Land-use and planning requirements.
  • Electrical installation requirements.
  • Electrical safety requirements.
  • Fire-safety requirements.
  • Industrial-safety requirements where applicable.
  • Environmental requirements.
  • Water-use requirements where the technology uses water resources.
  • Structural engineering requirements.
  • Requirements applicable to the specific machinery and generating equipment.
Measures to Reduce Licensing Risk

To maintain the proposed project as a genuine private off-grid self-consumption installation, We recommend that the project be designed and operated so that:

  • The generating installation has no physical connection to the public electricity network.
  • No electricity is imported from the public electricity network.
  • No electricity is exported to the public electricity network.
  • No electricity is sold to third parties.
  • No electricity is purchased from the public electricity network.
  • No participation in electricity trading is undertaken.
  • No electricity is supplied through a public electricity distribution network.
  • Electricity is used exclusively for internal household, industrial or corporate consumption.
  • The installation operates as an independent electrical island.
  • Electrical protection prevents accidental energisation of the public network.
  • Technical documentation clearly identifies the installation as an isolated self-consumption system.
  • The installed electrical capacity is documented and declared accurately.
  • Applicable construction, environmental, electrical and safety requirements are verified before commissioning.
Maximum Electrical Power
Identified statutory capacity threshold: No specific kW/MW threshold identified in the reviewed Belarusian legislation for a completely isolated electricity-generation facility used exclusively for internal self-consumption.

We have reviewed the available Belarusian electricity and licensing framework for the purpose of identifying a specific numerical capacity threshold applicable to an electricity-generation installation that:

  • operates completely off-grid;
  • does not import electricity;
  • does not export electricity;
  • does not sell electricity;
  • does not purchase electricity from the public network; and
  • produces electricity solely for internal consumption.

We have not identified a Belarusian statutory provision establishing a specific maximum installed electrical capacity in kW or MW solely for this configuration.

Belarusian regulatory materials distinguish electricity generation for the electricity system from electricity generated by enterprises for their own needs.

Belarusian energy-sector materials have also identified block-stations of 25 MW and above in the context of wholesale electricity-market participation. This figure should not be interpreted as a maximum or exemption threshold for an isolated self-consumption installation.

Important: We should not publish a numerical kW/MW maximum for Belarus for the specific off-grid configuration unless the competent Belarusian authority confirms such a threshold in the legislation applicable to the proposed technology and installation.

The applicable capacity may nevertheless affect other regulatory regimes, including construction, industrial safety, environmental protection, electrical safety, land use and, where applicable, water-resource regulation.

No specific statutory kW/MW maximum identified for the reviewed purely off-grid, self-consumption-only configuration.

Overview

We are considering a gravity-powered low-carbon electricity generation facility located in Belgium and operated exclusively for internal self-consumption.

The intended installation is designed to operate independently from the public electricity network, without importing electricity from or exporting electricity to the public electricity grid.

Electricity would be used exclusively for internal household, industrial or corporate electricity requirements under the control of the producer.

Belgian electricity legislation distinguishes electricity production from electricity transmission, distribution and supply and establishes a specific federal framework for electricity production.

Belgian electricity regulation is divided between federal and regional authorities. The federal framework applies in particular to electricity production, while the Regions are responsible for important matters concerning environmental, planning, construction and local energy regulation.

The federal Law of 29 April 1999 on the organisation of the electricity market establishes the principal framework applicable to electricity production.

The Belgian framework expressly defines an "autoproducer" as a natural or legal person producing electricity mainly for its own use. Therefore, the fact that an installation is intended exclusively for internal self-consumption does not by itself remove the installation from the electricity-production regulatory framework.

A completely isolated self-consumption installation must therefore be assessed as an electricity production installation while separately verifying the applicable regional construction, environmental, planning, safety and site-specific requirements.

Administrative Requirements

We should not treat a completely off-grid installation as automatically exempt from Belgian electricity-production requirements.

Belgian law expressly includes an "autoproducer" within the definition of a producer. Consequently, electricity generated primarily for the producer's own use remains relevant to the electricity-production regulatory framework.

Federal Electricity Production Framework

Under Article 4 of the Law of 29 April 1999 on the organisation of the electricity market, the establishment of new electricity production installations is in principle subject to prior individual authorisation.

The King may, under the conditions established by the applicable regulations, exempt low-power electricity production installations from the individual authorisation requirement and subject them instead to a prior declaration procedure.

The current CREG guidance identifies the applicable exemption threshold as a net developable capacity of 25 MWe .

New electricity production installations with a net developable capacity less than or equal to 25 MWe are exempt from the individual federal production authorisation.

However, installations within this threshold remain subject to a prior declaration to the CREG and the federal Minister for Energy or the minister's delegated authority.

25 MWe Federal Threshold

The relevant federal threshold for a new electricity production installation is:

Maximum power covered by the federal authorisation exemption:

25 MWe
Net developable capacity

An installation with a net developable capacity of up to and including 25 MWe does not require the individual federal electricity-production authorisation referred to in Article 4 of the Law of 29 April 1999.

Instead, the installation must be subject to the applicable prior declaration procedure to the CREG and the federal Minister for Energy or the delegated authority.

An installation exceeding 25 MWe falls outside this federal authorisation exemption and requires an individual production authorisation.

Regional Requirements

The federal 25 MWe threshold does not replace regional permitting requirements.

Belgium is divided into three Regions for important aspects of environmental, planning, construction and local energy regulation:

  • Flemish Region
  • Walloon Region
  • Brussels-Capital Region

Depending on the location and characteristics of the installation, additional permits, authorisations, notifications or environmental approvals may therefore be required.

The regional requirements must be checked independently from the federal 25 MWe electricity-production threshold.

Other Potential Administrative Requirements
  • Prior federal declaration where the installation falls within the 25 MWe exemption threshold.
  • Individual federal electricity-production authorisation where the installation exceeds the applicable 25 MWe threshold.
  • Regional environmental authorisation or permit, where applicable.
  • Construction and building-law requirements.
  • Land-use and spatial-planning requirements.
  • Electrical safety requirements.
  • Fire-safety requirements.
  • Occupational health and safety requirements.
  • Environmental requirements.
  • Water-law authorisation where the installation uses water resources.
  • Structural engineering requirements.
  • Additional requirements arising from the particular gravity-powered technology and the characteristics of the site.
Measures to Reduce Licensing Risk

For a project intended to remain a genuinely isolated self-consumption installation, We recommend that:

  • The electricity-generation installation has no physical connection to the Belgian public electricity network.
  • No electricity is imported from the public grid.
  • No electricity is exported to the public grid.
  • No electricity is sold to third parties.
  • No electricity is purchased from the public grid.
  • No participation in electricity trading is undertaken.
  • No participation in electricity balancing or aggregation markets is undertaken.
  • Electricity is used exclusively for internal household, industrial or corporate self-consumption.
  • The installation operates independently in island mode.
  • Electrical protection prevents accidental connection to or energisation of the public grid.
  • The installation is documented as a private self-consumption facility.
  • The net developable electrical capacity is determined and documented in accordance with the applicable Belgian regulatory methodology.
  • The applicable federal declaration procedure is completed where the installation has a net developable capacity of up to 25 MWe.
  • An individual federal production authorisation is obtained where the installation exceeds 25 MWe.
  • The applicable regional environmental, construction and planning requirements are verified before construction.
  • The project's technology-specific safety, structural, environmental and operational requirements are independently verified.
Maximum Electrical Power
Belgium — Federal electricity-production threshold:

25 MWe
Net developable capacity

The current Belgian federal electricity-production framework establishes a specific threshold of 25 megawatts electrical (MWe) of net developable capacity.

New electricity production installations with a net developable capacity less than or equal to 25 MWe are exempt from the individual federal electricity-production authorisation.

This exemption does not mean that the installation can be constructed without administrative formalities. A prior declaration must be submitted to the CREG and to the federal Minister for Energy or the competent delegated authority.

Installation up to 25 MWe

Where the net developable capacity is ≤ 25 MWe , the installation benefits from the federal exemption from the individual production authorisation.

The applicable prior declaration procedure remains required.

The 25 MWe threshold is therefore the key federal capacity threshold to use for the classification of the proposed installation.

Installation above 25 MWe

Where the net developable capacity exceeds 25 MWe , the installation is outside the federal exemption and requires an individual electricity-production authorisation.

The authorisation is issued by the federal Minister responsible for Energy following the procedure involving the CREG.

The relevant federal capacity threshold for a new electricity-production installation is 25 MWe of net developable capacity.

Installations with a net developable capacity of ≤ 25 MWe are exempt from the individual federal production authorisation but remain subject to the applicable prior declaration procedure.

Installations exceeding 25 MWe require an individual federal electricity-production authorisation.

For a gravity-powered electricity-generation project, the 25 MWe threshold should therefore be used as the principal federal electricity-production threshold. The project's exact permitting position must then be assessed according to the Region, technology, installation design, site, environmental characteristics and other applicable legislation.

Overview

We are considering a gravity-powered low-carbon electricity generation facility located in Bosnia and Herzegovina and operated exclusively for internal self-consumption.

The intended installation is designed to operate independently from the public electricity network, without importing electricity from or exporting electricity to the public electricity grid.

Electricity would be used exclusively for internal household, industrial or corporate electricity requirements under the control of the producer.

Bosnia and Herzegovina does not have a single unified electricity-production licensing regime applicable throughout the entire territory. Electricity production is regulated primarily at the level of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Republika Srpska and Brčko District of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

Consequently, the applicable administrative requirements depend principally on the territorial location of the proposed installation.

In the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina and Republika Srpska, electricity production exclusively for the producer's own needs is treated differently from electricity production carried out as a regulated electricity-production activity.

Brčko District has its own electricity legislation and regulatory framework administered principally by the State Electricity Regulatory Commission (DERK).

A completely isolated self-consumption installation must therefore be assessed according to the entity or district in which it is located, while remaining subject to applicable construction, planning, environmental, safety, technical and other site-specific requirements.

Administrative Requirements

We should not treat a completely off-grid installation as automatically exempt from all administrative requirements in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

The applicable requirements depend on whether the facility is located in the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Republika Srpska or Brčko District.

Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina

The Law on Electricity of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, published in the Official Gazette of the Federation of BiH No. 60/23, regulates electricity production, construction of power plants, licensing and related electricity-sector activities.

Article 17 provides that an electricity-sector entity is not required to hold a production licence for:

  • electricity production in power plants with installed capacity up to 1 MW;
  • electricity production exclusively for its own needs without delivery to the distribution network; and
  • electricity production in new power plants for a maximum of six months after obtaining the use permit.

The own-consumption exemption is therefore particularly relevant to a genuinely isolated installation that does not deliver electricity to the distribution network.

The same law separately regulates the energy permit required for construction of electricity-generation facilities.

Under Article 42, an energy permit is generally required before construction of a power plant. The law provides an exemption for plants with installed capacity below 1 MW , except for hydroelectric plants.

Consequently, the 1 MW figure is an important construction and regulatory threshold in the Federation, but it should not be described as a universal production-capacity ceiling for own-consumption generation.

Republika Srpska

Republika Srpska regulates electricity production through its electricity and energy legislation and the Regulatory Commission for Energy of Republika Srpska (RERS).

The applicable framework exempts electricity production carried out exclusively for the producer's own needs from the production licence requirement.

Electricity production in facilities with installed capacity up to 1 MW is also specifically identified as a category not requiring a production licence.

Where the same producer operates several facilities whose combined installed capacity exceeds 1 MW, the 1 MW exemption applicable to multiple small facilities does not apply.

Separate construction, environmental, spatial-planning and technical requirements remain applicable to the facility.

Brčko District

Brčko District has its own Law on Electricity and is regulated in the electricity sector by the State Electricity Regulatory Commission (DERK).

The Brčko District electricity framework provides a specific threshold of 1 MW for electricity-production licensing.

Production facilities with capacity up to 1 MW are exempt from the DERK production licence requirement under the applicable conditions.

The law also provides a specific procedure for electricity production for own needs with installed capacity up to 1 MW .

For facilities exceeding the applicable 1 MW threshold, the production licensing and construction authorisation framework of DERK applies.

Construction, technical, environmental, planning and other applicable requirements must nevertheless be verified separately.

  • Electricity-production licence where required by the applicable entity or district legislation.
  • Energy or construction authorisation, where applicable.
  • Construction and building-law requirements.
  • Land-use and spatial-planning requirements.
  • Environmental authorisation or permit, where applicable.
  • Electrical safety requirements.
  • Fire-safety requirements.
  • Occupational health and safety requirements.
  • Water-law authorisation where the installation uses water resources.
  • Structural engineering requirements.
  • Technical approval and inspection requirements.
  • Possible concession requirements, depending on the land, energy source and project characteristics.
  • Additional requirements arising from the particular technology and site.
Measures to Reduce Licensing Risk

For a project intended to remain a genuinely isolated self-consumption installation, We recommend that:

  • The electricity-generation installation has no physical connection to the public electricity network.
  • No electricity is imported from the public grid.
  • No electricity is exported to the public grid.
  • No electricity is sold to third parties.
  • No electricity is purchased from the public grid.
  • No electricity is supplied to third parties.
  • No participation in electricity trading is undertaken.
  • No participation in electricity balancing or aggregation markets is undertaken.
  • Electricity is used exclusively for internal household, industrial or corporate self-consumption.
  • The installation operates independently in island mode.
  • Electrical protection prevents accidental connection to or energisation of the public grid.
  • The installed electrical capacity is documented and verified by a qualified electrical engineer.
  • The applicable territorial framework is identified before construction: Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Republika Srpska or Brčko District.
  • The 1 MW regulatory threshold is checked against the applicable electricity-production, construction and permitting provisions.
  • Any required energy, construction, environmental, planning, water or technical authorisations are obtained before construction or operation.
  • The installation is documented as a private self-consumption facility rather than a facility intended for electricity supply or commercial electricity sales.
Maximum Electrical Power
Bosnia and Herzegovina — principal capacity threshold:

1 MW
Principal installed-capacity threshold used in the electricity-production licensing and construction framework.

Bosnia and Herzegovina does not apply a single electricity-production licensing law uniformly to all parts of the country.

The applicable framework depends on whether the installation is located in the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Republika Srpska or Brčko District.

Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina

The Federation's Law on Electricity establishes 1 MW as an important installed-capacity threshold.

Electricity-production facilities with installed capacity up to 1 MW are exempt from the ordinary production-licence requirement.

In addition, electricity production exclusively for the producer's own needs without delivery to the distribution network is expressly exempted from the production-licence requirement.

Article 42 separately provides that an energy permit is not required for construction of electricity-generation facilities with installed capacity below 1 MW , except for hydroelectric plants.

For a gravity-powered facility that is not a hydroelectric plant, 1 MW is therefore the key federal installed-capacity threshold for the construction-permit analysis.

Republika Srpska

Republika Srpska uses 1 MW as the principal threshold for electricity production licensing.

Electricity production exclusively for own needs is exempt from the production licence requirement under the applicable legislation.

Electricity production in facilities up to 1 MW is also specifically identified as exempt from the production licence requirement.

Separate construction, environmental and planning approvals may nevertheless apply.

Brčko District

Brčko District establishes a specific 1 MW threshold for electricity-production licensing.

Production facilities up to 1 MW fall within the statutory exemption from the DERK electricity-production licence under the applicable conditions.

The Brčko District framework also provides a specific procedure for production of electricity for own needs with installed capacity up to 1 MW .

Facilities exceeding 1 MW require the applicable DERK production licensing and construction authorisation procedures.

Website classification for Bosnia and Herzegovina:

Principal capacity threshold: 1 MW

The 1 MW threshold is the principal installed-capacity figure identified in the electricity-production licensing and construction framework of the relevant Bosnian regulatory jurisdictions.

For the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina and Republika Srpska, electricity production exclusively for the producer's own needs is subject to specific statutory treatment and is not subject to the ordinary production-licence requirement when the applicable statutory conditions are satisfied.

In Brčko District, the legislation specifically provides for own-needs electricity production up to 1 MW and establishes the corresponding administrative procedure.

For the comparative database, the appropriate figure to record for Bosnia and Herzegovina is therefore 1 MW as the principal installed-capacity threshold, with the important qualification that the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina and Republika Srpska contain separate exemptions for electricity production exclusively for own needs. The precise permitting position must be determined from the law applicable to the specific location of the facility.

This information is provided for general public information purposes only. Bosnia and Herzegovina has a territorially divided electricity regulatory framework, and the precise requirements applicable to a gravity-powered electricity-generation facility depend on whether the installation is located in the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Republika Srpska or Brčko District. The 1 MW figure identified on this page is the principal installed-capacity threshold appearing in the relevant electricity-production licensing and construction frameworks. It must not be interpreted as eliminating other permits or authorisations. In particular, construction, planning, environmental, water, technical, fire-safety, structural, occupational-safety and other requirements may apply independently of the electricity-production licence. For installations intended exclusively for internal self-consumption and physically isolated from the public electricity network, the applicable own-consumption exemption should be assessed under the legislation of the specific territory in which the facility is located. Overview

We are considering a gravity-powered low-carbon electricity generation facility located in Bulgaria and operated exclusively for internal self-consumption.

The intended installation is designed to operate independently from the public electricity network, without importing electricity from or exporting electricity to the public electricity grid.

Electricity would be used exclusively for internal household, industrial or corporate electricity requirements under the control of the producer.

Bulgarian electricity production is principally regulated by the Bulgarian Energy Act (Energy Act) and, where the installation qualifies as a renewable energy installation, by the Energy from Renewable Sources Act.

The Energy Act establishes electricity production as an activity subject to licensing, while expressly providing exemptions for certain electricity production facilities.

The current Bulgarian Energy Act provides that an electricity production licence is not required for a person owning a power plant with a total installed electrical capacity of up to and including 20 MW .

The Energy Act also separately provides that a licence is not required for electricity generation for self-consumption only , including electricity generation by citizen energy communities and active customers.

A completely isolated self-consumption installation must therefore be assessed under both provisions, together with the applicable construction, spatial planning, environmental, electrical safety and technology-specific requirements.

Administrative Requirements

We should not treat a completely off-grid installation as automatically exempt from all Bulgarian administrative requirements.

The electricity-production licensing provisions, construction legislation, spatial-planning rules, environmental requirements and electrical safety requirements must be assessed separately.

Electricity Production Licence

Article 39 of the Bulgarian Energy Act lists electricity production among the activities subject to licensing.

However, Article 39(4)(1) expressly provides that an electricity production licence is not required for a person owning a power plant with a total installed electrical capacity of up to and including 20 MW .

This threshold was increased from 5 MW to 20 MW by the amendment published in State Gazette No. 11 of 2 February 2023.

Consequently, the current Bulgarian electricity-production licensing threshold is 20 MW , not 5 MW.

Self-Consumption Exemption

The Bulgarian Energy Act contains a separate exemption for electricity generation for self-consumption only .

Article 39(4)(5) provides that a licence is not required for electricity generation for self-consumption only, including electricity generation by citizen energy communities and active customers.

This provision is particularly relevant to the proposed operating configuration because the installation is intended to be physically isolated from the public electricity network.

No electricity would be imported, exported, sold or supplied to third parties.

The self-consumption exemption must nevertheless be read together with the construction, environmental, spatial-planning and technical requirements applicable to the project.

Renewable Energy Self-Consumption Rules

Where a generation installation qualifies as an electricity-production installation from a renewable energy source, additional provisions of the Energy from Renewable Sources Act may apply.

Article 25a of the Energy from Renewable Sources Act provides a special procedure for certain renewable-energy installations built on roofs, facades and associated properties in urbanised areas where the electricity is intended solely for own consumption.

Under that provision, the total installed capacity may be up to twice the supplied capacity of the customer but may not exceed 5 MW .

This 5 MW threshold is specific to the Article 25a renewable-energy self-consumption regime and must not be confused with the general electricity-production licensing threshold under Article 39 of the Energy Act.

Because the proposed technology is a gravity-powered system rather than automatically one of the renewable sources defined by the Bulgarian renewable-energy legislation, the applicability of Article 25a must be confirmed from the technical characteristics and legal classification of the actual installation.

  • Technical commissioning and operational requirements.
  • Additional requirements arising from the specific technology and location.
Measures to Reduce Licensing Risk

For a project intended to remain a genuinely isolated self-consumption installation, We recommend that:

  • The electricity-generation installation has no physical connection to the Bulgarian public electricity network.
  • No electricity is imported from the public grid.
  • No electricity is exported to the public grid.
  • No electricity is sold to third parties.
  • No electricity is purchased from the public grid.
  • No electricity is supplied to third parties.
  • No participation in electricity trading is undertaken.
  • No participation in balancing or aggregation markets is undertaken.
  • Electricity is used exclusively for internal household, industrial or corporate self-consumption.
  • The installation operates independently in island mode.
  • Electrical protection prevents accidental connection to or energisation of the public grid.
  • The installed electrical capacity is clearly documented and verified by a qualified electrical engineer.
  • The project is assessed under Article 39 of the Bulgarian Energy Act before construction.
  • The separate self-consumption exemption under Article 39(4)(5) is documented where applicable.
  • The 20 MW installed-capacity threshold is checked against the applicable production-licensing provisions.
  • Where the installation qualifies as renewable energy, the applicability of the Energy from Renewable Sources Act is separately verified.
  • Construction, environmental, spatial-planning, water, fire-safety and technical requirements are independently verified before construction.
Maximum Electrical Power
Bulgaria — general electricity-production licensing threshold:

20 MW
Total installed electrical capacity

The current Bulgarian Energy Act provides that an electricity-production licence is not required for a person owning a power plant with a total installed electrical capacity of up to and including 20 MW .

This is the current threshold following the amendment published in State Gazette No. 11 of 2 February 2023, which increased the previous threshold from 5 MW to 20 MW.

The Bulgarian Agency for Sustainable Energy Development confirms in its renewable-energy procedures handbook that a production licence is required only for electricity-production facilities with a total installed electrical capacity above 20 MW .

Installation up to 20 MW

A power plant with a total installed electrical capacity of up to and including 20 MW does not require the electricity-production licence referred to in Article 39 of the Energy Act.

This threshold applies to the general electricity-production licensing exemption.

Other permits and administrative requirements may nevertheless apply to construction and operation of the facility.

Installation above 20 MW

Where a power plant has a total installed electrical capacity above 20 MW , the general exemption in Article 39(4)(1) no longer applies.

Electricity production then falls within the ordinary production-licensing framework of the Bulgarian Energy Act, unless another statutory exemption applies.

The separate statutory exemption for electricity production for self-consumption only must also be assessed under Article 39(4)(5).

Special Renewable Self-Consumption Threshold

A separate 5 MW threshold exists under Article 25a of the Energy from Renewable Sources Act for certain renewable-energy self-consumption installations located on or associated with buildings in urbanised areas.

Under this specific regime, the total installed capacity may be up to twice the supplied capacity but may not exceed 5 MW .

This 5 MW threshold is not the general electricity-production licensing threshold and should only be used where the project satisfies the specific conditions of Article 25a.

Website classification for Bulgaria:

General electricity-production threshold: 20 MW

Electricity-production installations with a total installed electrical capacity of up to and including 20 MW are exempt from the general electricity-production licence under Article 39(4)(1) of the Bulgarian Energy Act.

A separate exemption applies to electricity generation for self-consumption only under Article 39(4)(5).

For certain renewable-energy self-consumption installations covered by Article 25a of the Energy from Renewable Sources Act, a separate 5 MW capacity limit applies to that specific simplified regime.

For the comparative database, the appropriate primary Bulgarian figure is therefore 20 MW of total installed electrical capacity. The 20 MW figure is the current general electricity-production licensing threshold. The project's completely isolated self-consumption configuration must additionally be assessed under the separate own-consumption exemption in Article 39(4)(5).

  6. Amendment to the Energy Act, State Gazette No. 11 of 2 February 2023 — increased the general electricity-production licence exemption threshold from 5 MW to 20 MW .

  8. Energy from Renewable Sources Act — Article 25a — special self-consumption regime for certain renewable-energy installations associated with buildings and urbanised properties, subject to a capacity limit of 5 MW and other statutory conditions.
  9. Energy and Water Regulatory Commission (EWRC / КЕВР) — Bulgarian electricity and energy regulatory authority.
  10. Agency for Sustainable Energy Development (ASED / АУЕР) — Bulgarian authority responsible for renewable-energy administration and related procedures.
Public Information Notice

This information is provided for general public information purposes only. We recommend verifying the legislation, regulations, registrations, notifications, authorisations, permits and administrative procedures applicable to the proposed Bulgarian facility before development, construction or operation. Under the current Bulgarian Energy Act, the general electricity-production licensing threshold is 20 MW of total installed electrical capacity. The Bulgarian Energy Act additionally contains a separate exemption for electricity generation for self-consumption only. Where the project qualifies as a renewable-energy installation, the Energy from Renewable Sources Act may introduce additional procedures and, for specific building-associated self-consumption projects, a separate 5 MW threshold under Article 25a. The exact legal classification of a gravity-powered installation depends on its technical design, energy source, installed electrical capacity, operating configuration, connection status, location, land use and actual use of the electricity. Construction, environmental, spatial-planning, electrical safety, fire-safety, structural and other requirements may apply independently of the electricity-production licensing exemption.

Overview

We are considering a gravity-powered low-carbon electricity generation facility located in Croatia and operated exclusively for internal self-consumption.

The intended installation is designed to operate independently from the public electricity network, without importing electricity from or exporting electricity to the public electricity grid.

Electricity would be used exclusively for internal household, industrial or corporate electricity requirements under the control of the producer.

Croatian electricity production is principally regulated by the Electricity Market Act (Zakon o tržištu električne energije), together with the Energy Act and other legislation applicable to energy infrastructure.

The Electricity Market Act regulates electricity production, transmission, distribution, supply, market activities and the rights and obligations of electricity producers and consumers.

Croatian legislation expressly allows electricity production without an electricity-production licence in certain circumstances, including production using generating facilities whose combined installed capacity is up to and including 1 MW .

The same provision separately allows electricity production exclusively for the producer's own needs without an electricity-production licence.

A completely isolated self-consumption installation must therefore be assessed primarily under the electricity-production exemption, together with applicable construction, spatial-planning, environmental, electrical-safety, fire-safety and technology-specific requirements.

Administrative Requirements

We should not treat a completely off-grid installation as automatically exempt from all Croatian administrative requirements.

The electricity-production licensing provisions must be considered separately from construction, spatial-planning, environmental, technical and safety requirements.

Electricity Production Licence

Under Article 10 of the Croatian Electricity Market Act, electricity production is normally an electricity-market activity requiring the appropriate authorisation.

Article 10(2), however, provides an exemption allowing legal or natural persons to carry out electricity production without an electricity-market activity licence where they ensure professional management and operation of the energy facilities in accordance with the applicable technical requirements.

One of the express exemptions covers electricity production using generating facilities whose total installed capacities are up to and including 1 MW .

This establishes 1 MW as the principal installed-capacity threshold relevant to the general licence exemption.

Self-Consumption Exemption

Article 10(2) contains a separate exemption for electricity production exclusively for the producer's own needs .

This is particularly relevant to the proposed configuration because the installation is intended to be completely isolated from the public electricity network.

Under the proposed configuration:

  • No electricity would be imported from the public grid.
  • No electricity would be exported to the public grid.
  • No electricity would be sold to third parties.
  • Electricity would be used exclusively for the producer's own requirements.

The own-needs exemption therefore provides a particularly relevant legal basis for a genuinely isolated self-consumption installation.

Renewable Energy Considerations

Croatia has a separate legislative framework for electricity produced from renewable energy sources and high-efficiency cogeneration.

The Croatian renewable-energy legislation contains specific rules concerning self-consumption, renewable-energy consumers and electricity-production installations.

However, a gravity-powered generation system should not automatically be classified as a renewable-energy installation merely because gravity is used as the mechanical principle for electricity generation.

The legal classification depends on the actual source of the energy used by the installation.

If the installation uses a renewable energy source recognized by Croatian legislation, the renewable-energy self-consumption provisions may additionally apply.

For a generic gravity-powered facility, the Electricity Market Act should therefore be used as the principal electricity-production licensing reference unless the actual technology qualifies separately under the renewable-energy legislation.

  • Electrical safety requirements.

  • Occupational health and safety requirements.
  • Structural engineering requirements.
  • Water-law requirements where water resources or hydraulic infrastructure are used.
  • Technical inspection and commissioning requirements.
  • Additional requirements arising from the specific technology and location.
Measures to Reduce Licensing Risk

For a project intended to remain a genuinely isolated self-consumption installation, We recommend that:

  • The electricity-generation installation has no physical connection to the Croatian public electricity network.
  • No electricity is imported from the public grid.
  • No electricity is exported to the public grid.
  • No electricity is sold to third parties.
  • No electricity is purchased from the public grid.
  • No electricity is supplied to third parties.
  • No participation in electricity trading is undertaken.
  • No participation in electricity balancing or aggregation markets is undertaken.
  • Electricity is used exclusively for internal household, industrial or corporate self-consumption.
  • The installation operates independently in island mode.
  • Electrical protection prevents accidental connection to or energisation of the public grid.
  • The total installed electrical capacity is documented and verified by a qualified electrical engineer.
  • The 1 MW installed-capacity threshold is checked against the applicable electricity-production licensing provisions.
  • The separate exemption for electricity production exclusively for own needs is documented and assessed.
  • If the technology is claimed to use renewable energy, the renewable-energy classification is verified separately.
  • Construction, environmental, spatial-planning, water, fire-safety and technical requirements are independently verified before construction.

Croatia — principal installed-capacity threshold:

1 MW
Total installed electrical capacity

Article 10(2) of the Croatian Electricity Market Act permits electricity production without an electricity-market activity licence where the production facilities have a combined installed capacity of up to and including 1 MW , subject to the statutory technical-management requirements.

The same Article 10(2) separately permits electricity production exclusively for the producer's own needs without the electricity-production licence.

Installation up to 1 MW

A production installation or combination of production facilities with a total installed capacity of up to and including 1 MW falls within the statutory electricity production licence exemption.

The producer must nevertheless ensure professional management and operation of the energy facilities in accordance with applicable technical requirements.

Construction, spatial-planning, environmental, electrical and safety requirements remain separately applicable.

Completely Isolated Self-Consumption

The Croatian legislation contains a separate exemption for electricity production exclusively for the producer's own needs .

This exemption is particularly relevant where the installation is completely isolated from the public electricity network and does not import or export electricity.

The legal analysis should therefore distinguish between:

  • the general 1 MW installed-capacity exemption; and
  • the separate exemption for production exclusively for own needs.

The 1 MW figure should consequently be treated as the principal capacity threshold for the general licensing analysis rather than as a technology-specific physical limit on the proposed gravity-generation system.

Renewable Self-Consumption — Separate Regime

Croatia's renewable-energy legislation contains additional rules for electricity produced from renewable sources for self-consumption.

The current legislation also provides a specific 6 MW limit for certain renewable-energy self-consumption production installations located at a remote location behind other metering points.

This 6 MW threshold applies only to that specific statutory renewable-energy self-consumption configuration.

It should not be substituted for the general 1 MW electricity-production licence threshold when assessing a generic, completely isolated gravity-powered electricity-generation facility.

Overview

We are considering a gravity-powered low-carbon electricity generation facility located in Cyprus and operated exclusively for internal self-consumption.

The intended installation is designed to operate independently from the public electricity network, without importing electricity from or exporting electricity to the public electricity grid.

Electricity would be used exclusively for internal household, industrial or corporate electricity requirements under the control of the producer.

Electricity generation in Cyprus is regulated by the Laws Regulating the Electricity Market and the regulatory framework administered by the Cyprus Energy Regulatory Authority (CERA).

The Cypriot electricity licensing framework distinguishes between electricity generation for commercial purposes, electricity generation for own use, generation using renewable energy sources and generation from autonomous power plants that are not connected to the transmission or distribution system.

CERA's current General Licence framework expressly includes electricity generation from power plants that are not connected to the transmission or distribution system.

CERA also provides a specific licence-exemption regime for electricity generation for own use from systems with an electrical capacity greater than 30 kW and up to 1 MW .

For renewable-energy electricity generation, CERA provides a separate exemption framework covering renewable-energy power plants from more than 50 kW up to and including 8 MW , subject to the conditions of that regime.

A completely isolated gravity-powered installation must therefore be classified according to its actual technology and energy source. The 1 MW own-use threshold is the appropriate principal capacity figure for a generic non-RES self-consumption classification, while the 8 MW threshold applies specifically to the statutory RES exemption.

Administrative Requirements

We should not treat an off-grid installation as automatically exempt from all Cypriot administrative requirements.

Cyprus has a specific regulatory framework for autonomous electricity-generation installations, electricity generation for own use and renewable energy generation.

Autonomous / Off-Grid Generation

Article 27 of the Laws Regulating the Electricity Market provides for a General Licence covering generation of electricity from power plants that are not connected to the transmission or distribution system.

CERA's current General Licence information also expressly identifies Autonomous generator as a General Licence category.

This is directly relevant to the proposed configuration because the facility is intended to operate as a completely independent electrical island.

The autonomous status must nevertheless be established through the applicable CERA regulatory procedure and does not remove construction, environmental, safety or other statutory requirements.

Electricity Generation for Own Use

CERA provides a specific exemption from the obligation to hold a licence for generation of electricity for own use from systems with a capacity greater than 30 kW and up to 1 MW .

CERA's current licensing information expressly identifies this category as an exemption from the obligation to hold a licence.

This regime is particularly relevant where electricity is generated exclusively for the producer's own requirements.

The 1 MW threshold is therefore the principal capacity figure to use for a generic non-RES own-use installation.

Renewable Energy Generation

CERA provides a separate exemption regime for electricity generation stations using renewable energy sources.

The current regime covers electricity generation stations using any RES technology with an installed capacity from 50 kW up to and including 8 MW .

CERA's current licensing information states that construction and operation licences apply to RES generation stations exceeding 8 MW .

However, the proposed gravity-powered system should not automatically be classified as RES merely because gravity is used as the mechanical operating principle.

The 8 MW threshold should therefore only be applied if the actual installation qualifies as a renewable-energy power plant under Cypriot legislation.

For a project intended to remain a genuinely isolated self-consumption installation, We recommend that:

  • The electricity-generation installation has no physical connection to the Cypriot transmission or distribution network.
  • No electricity is imported from the public grid.
  • No electricity is exported to the public grid.
  • No electricity is sold to third parties.
  • No electricity is purchased from the public grid.
  • No electricity is supplied to third parties.
  • No participation in electricity trading is undertaken.
  • No participation in balancing or aggregation markets is undertaken.
  • Electricity is used exclusively for internal household, industrial or corporate self-consumption.
  • The installation operates as an autonomous electrical island.
  • Electrical protection prevents accidental connection to or energisation of the public grid.
  • The installed electrical capacity is documented and verified by a qualified electrical engineer.
  • The 1 MW own-use threshold is checked where the installation is classified as a non-RES self-consumption generator.
  • If the installation is claimed to use a renewable energy source, the RES classification is verified separately.
  • The applicability of the CERA autonomous-generator General Licence is verified before construction.
